audit: Independent novelty and existing-hardware boundary audit for Granite4Htiny complementary g12 row striping
scope: Read-only audit of frozen training-selected virtual layouts and primary literature. No author source or plan edited. No heldout route or heldout summary opened by this auditor.

verdict.summary_zh: g12 的完整 row 與地址配置在本模型內通過獨立核對；但是 overlapping/complement mask 結構已有 staggered striping 先例，query-coactivation/step-cost/minmax 已有 declustering 先例。尚無證據支持論文新穎性已成立。可繼續檢驗的是合法 NAND whole-row 分片與輸入/輸出/command 成本下，相對同樣幾何與同樣查詢資訊的強基線，是否還有穩健可泛化的增益。
verdict.do_not_infer: No exact identical full algorithm was verified; absence of a found exact paper is not novelty clearance.

frozen_evidence.critical_baseline_correction: Strong group down layout is 35 layers group_g16 and 5 layers group_g4, not all forty layers g16. GU has 21 group_g8 and 19 complement_g8, the latter being equivalent disjoint halves.
frozen_evidence.timing_evidence_limit: Training routed-projection service model only; neither real-device timing nor full-model inference latency. Published AiF internal ECC bandwidth does not itself calibrate MAC throughput.

mathematical_prior_reductions.name: cyclic overlap masks
mathematical_prior_reductions.construction: Arrange chips 0..15 on a ring. Four length-12 windows starting at 0,4,8,12 omit exactly the four length-4 aligned groups, up to a cyclic relabeling.
mathematical_prior_reductions.conclusion: The mask family is not new; training the assignment of experts to these masks is a distinct detail that still needs comparison against query-aware declustering.

mathematical_prior_reductions.name: fixed geometry-matched atoms
mathematical_prior_reductions.construction: Before placement, represent each 1536×512 INT8 down matrix as twelve 128×512 whole-row atoms. Each atom occupies 64KiB = four 16KiB pages = one four-plane wave. A top6 query requests 72 atoms.
mathematical_prior_reductions.conclusion: Its expected maximum device-sum objective already describes this cost after restricting one expert to at most one atom per chip. Merely changing from sixteen 96-row items to twelve 128-row items does not evade this prior; atoms can be defined at the new geometry from the start.

mathematical_prior_reductions.name: selected-set occupancy
mathematical_prior_reductions.construction: Let n_g be how many of the six selected experts omit group g. Each chip in group g executes 6−n_g waves, hence makespan is 6−min_g n_g. Since sum n_g=6 over four groups, min n_g is 0 or 1 and down has five or six waves.
mathematical_prior_reductions.conclusion: This is a useful exact characterization for the restricted four-mask family, not by itself a new general scheduling result.

capacity_and_command_audit.what_it_means: The existing WaveAllocator reserves complete four-plane waves and protects short streams from additional block crossings. New row geometry fills every wave and happens to fill every 192-WL block. Reported reservation differences are allocator policy plus shape occupancy, not fewer weight bytes.
capacity_and_command_audit.capacity_claim_boundary: 6.039797760 GB versus 6.845104128 GB is a comparison of these virtual wave-reserving layouts. It is not evidence of better weight compression or a capacity gain over the best legal FTL/dense allocator. Raw TLC covered bytes are three times reserved LSB bytes and are not the stored INT8 model size.
capacity_and_command_audit.unused_plane_boundary: The unused fourth-plane slot of a g16 three-page stream can hold other physical pages under a denser mapping. Whether they can be consumed at the same latency depends on legal command/address/input contexts. The published native operands do not establish independently chosen per-plane row offsets and simultaneous different expert input vectors. No free extra GEMV may be assumed.
capacity_and_command_audit.strong_baseline_requirement: Construct a legal page/row-dense g16 or 128-row-tile layout with explicit per-run addresses and charge any extra ordinary reads, native commands and input transfers. Compare capacity–commands–critical-path frontiers. A dense allocator may reach the same payload lower bound while trading service costs; that conditional possibility must not be declared either impossible or free.

compatible_at_primitive_level: Native INT8 GEMV on complete 128-row by512-column down shards
One existing full input vector per selected chip command
One-copy immutable weights; unchanged routing and nonlinear operations
Controller static shard map, targeted chip dispatch and full-row output concatenation
existing_hardware_boundary.software_work_needed: Published automatic aif_post is equal full-chip row mapping. A controller mapping/dispatcher must expose these proper subsets and concatenate row ranges. The repository currently materializes metadata, not programmed NAND or executable AiF physical commands.
not_supported_by_evidence: Free reuse of idle plane slots with unrelated vectors in one chip GEMV
Independent arbitrary per-plane block/WL command operands
More concurrent input contexts than disclosed
New raw-I32 output or codec modes
existing_hardware_boundary.no_precision_extension_required_by_rows: Whole-row partitioning does not require cross-chip partial dot-product sums; numeric identity still assumes the existing native GEMV executes the same rows and input accurately. This audit does not certify unimplemented quantization/PE details.

minimum_novelty_tests.baseline: Same g12, same balanced four masks, same allocator and exact service model, but uniform/random balanced expert assignment; include many seeds and frequency-only assignment.
minimum_novelty_tests.falsifies: If most gain remains with arbitrary balanced colors, attribute it to geometry/striping. Do not describe the full benefit as learned coactivation.

minimum_novelty_tests.baseline: Fixed 128-row atoms optimized using established weighted minmax declustering objective, same train queries/capacities and one-chip-per-expert constraints; restricted four-mask solver and a less restricted legal atom-placement solver.
minimum_novelty_tests.falsifies: If an ordinary existing declustering implementation or straightforward adaptation matches the result, the solver/assignment is not a new method. A NAND-specific cost correction still needs separate validation.

minimum_novelty_tests.baseline: All legal integer complete-row widths, phase-specific geometry, disjoint and cyclic overlapping masks, equal information budget. Compare against g4 down as well as g16 because the frozen strong baseline already chooses g4 for five layers.
minimum_novelty_tests.falsifies: If benefit comes only from selecting a previously omitted legal width, position it as baseline correction or model-specific geometry result rather than a novel placement principle.

minimum_novelty_tests.baseline: Existing whole-row native GEMV/offset primitives, explicit nonoverlap map, current software dispatcher, charge extra commands/input/onfi/output/ordinary waves.
minimum_novelty_tests.falsifies: If dense baseline erases reservation or latency difference, retire the corresponding capacity/throughput claim. Do not compare against only the old WaveAllocator padding.

minimum_novelty_tests.baseline: Parent-managed frozen new holdouts, uniform without-replacement routing, marginal-preserving shuffled routing, additional compatible tensor shapes/models, unchanged scheduler and precision.
minimum_novelty_tests.falsifies: If effects disappear outside one shape/routing set or under calibrated command/input costs, no broad flash-MoE paper claim follows.

communicated_not_recomputed_here.meaning: Every balanced assignment is equivalent under uniform expert sampling. This is a necessary null control, not evidence of learned generalization.

related_independent_agent_receipts.holdout_access: This literature auditor did not load heldout route files or heldout summary.

permitted_current_claims_zh: 在指定 ordinary-read／四-plane／完整-row 模型中，Granite 此 down shape 的 g12 配置可以消除 g16 每波一個 idle plane，且不增加權重 page 數。
凍結虛擬地址計畫通過 one-copy、row coverage、page overlap、block 邊界與 run-count 的獨立核對。
目前訓練模擬相對 phasewise 強 group baseline 有可量化收益；其一般性、真實硬體收益與論文新穎性仍需相應證據。
claims_not_supported_zh: 首次 overlapping／complement-group striping；首次以 coactivation／stepwise cost／minmax 作 placement。
6.04GB vs6.85GB 是相對 SOTA 的模型容量改善，或等同權重壓縮。
因 2001 item 是 atomic，而本法會 re-shard，所以本法自然落在既有 declustering 之外。
FlexLLM／DIAMoND 未使用相同 masks、whole-row partition 或 coactivation；其全文尚未取得，不能作此否定。
已達投稿突破，或已證明實際端到端 LLM speedup。

sources.title: Staggered striping in multimedia information systems
sources.version: Author-institution technical report dated 1993-12-09; conference publication 1994-05-24, verified publisher-registered Crossref metadata
sources.read_depth: Legal institutional scanned 26-page report downloaded; rendered and read printed pp.2–5 and 7–10, especially §3.2 and Fig.4. Not all evaluation pages read. Web screenshot timed out; local rendered pp.9–10 inspected.
sources.primary_evidence: §3.2 replaces disjoint physical disk clusters with overlapping logical clusters; successive subobjects shift by stride k around D disks. Degree M varies with object bandwidth. k=M recovers simple striping when D is divisible by M.
sources.our_inference: D=16, M=12, k=4 generates exactly the same four participating-chip subset masks as omitting one of four consecutive 4-chip groups. This is a structural mask-family equivalence, not evidence of the same learned expert assignment.
sources.limits: Multimedia subobjects and periodic streaming, not fixed MoE matrix shards, page-buffer GEMV, or learned selected-expert sets. Do not call the full g12 implementation identical.

sources.title: A Hypergraph Based Approach to Declustering Problems
sources.read_depth: Original 20-page full text available; read introduction, §2 Definitions1–6 and §3 formulation/greedy method through complexity discussion. Results not comprehensively audited.
sources.primary_evidence: Atomic items cannot be split across disks (p.270). Definitions model item sizes, device capacities, query frequencies and expected query response equal to the largest per-disk sum of item retrieval times. Definition4 explicitly permits retrieval time to be a step function of item size.
sources.our_inference: Fix each down expert as twelve 128-row, 64KiB atoms before optimization. A top6 query requests 72 atoms; minimizing largest chip atom count is directly a constrained instance of the existing objective. A distinct-chip-per-expert constraint and GEMV input/output costs are extra constraints, not automatic evidence of a new optimization principle.
sources.limits: Does not itself choose matrix row granularity or implement legal NAND GEMV addresses. Original model treats disk operations as independent and abstracts transfer/compute.

sources.title: AiF: Accelerating On-Device LLM Inference Using In-Flash Processing
sources.local_primary_fulltext: /home/ericyu/expert_flash_experiment/AiF - Accelerating On-Device LLM Inference Using In-Flash Processing.pdf
sources.read_depth: Original selected architecture, mapping, command-interface and evaluation sections checked in prior rounds; this round rechecked project evidence notes and native-command boundaries. §4.4 p.536; §5.2 pp.537–538 incl. footnotes8–9.
sources.primary_evidence: Chip GEMV operands include vector dimension, block ID, block offset and page count. Published host mapping equal-row partitions matrices across AiF chips. A submatrix crossing IFP blocks becomes multiple GEMVs. Simulator issues dummy computation results.
sources.our_inference: Static complete-row shards on 12 selected chips need controller mapping/dispatch/concat software, but no new multiply datatype or partial-dot reduction. The published automatic aif_post mapping is not itself an exposed arbitrary chip-mask API.
sources.limits: Per-plane independent row lists, independent concurrent input vectors, free hole coalescing and a measured MAC rate are not established by these interfaces. This is a legal-primitives argument, not an implemented-device validation.
sources.code: No AiF-specific public artifact verified; upstream NVMeVirt is not the full AiF implementation.

sources.title: Cambricon-LLM: A Chiplet-Based Hybrid Architecture for On-Device Inference of 70B LLM
sources.read_depth: Original §V-A/B reread this round; §IV–VII selectively read in previous rounds.
sources.primary_evidence: Hardware-aware tiling matches NAND page size and channel/core counts, optimizing input/result traffic. A tile is evenly distributed across all compute cores; channels split input width and within-channel cores split output rows. NPU/flash workload shares are chosen to balance execution.
sources.our_inference: Matrix tiling, row/column asymmetry, complete hardware geometry and transfer-aware partitioning are already prior. The inspected mapping is not evidence of learned proper-subset complement masks.
sources.limits: Custom compute cores, shared compute between two planes, on-die ECC, 2KiB buffers and hybrid NPU computation; not the same AiF primitive/plane context. Author-page FlashLLM naming here refers to this architecture, not the unrelated GPU Flash-LLM family.

sources.title: Cambricon-FlexLLM: A Flexible Chiplet-Based Hybrid Architecture for On-Device 70B LLM Inference
sources.version: Published online 2026-10-13. Publisher-registered print date 2026-12-31 is future relative to this audit.
sources.read_depth: Publisher-registered title/date/abstract fetched directly from Crossref. Official full/PDF/epdf inaccessible in earlier bounded access checks; no legal author preprint located. Full algorithm NOT read.
sources.primary_evidence: Registered abstract states hardware tiling plus co-activation-neuron-inspired weight reordering and sparsity-aware dynamic partitioning, to reduce transfers of ineffective weights.
sources.our_inference: Broad claims of first coactivation-based flash weight arrangement or first dynamic partitioning are unsafe. Exact overlap-mask equivalence cannot be confirmed or excluded from abstract.
sources.limits: Cannot infer complete-row sharding, chip masks, replicas, CR dependency, plane independence or precise execution costs. Treat as unresolved close prior, not a cleared comparison.

sources.title: Beyond Capacity: Scalable MoE LLM Inference via High-Bandwidth Flash with Direct GPU and HBM Paths
sources.venue: arXiv preprint; no peer-reviewed venue verified
sources.read_depth: Original §V-A/B, §VI-A and §VI-E read; related architecture/placement portions inspected in earlier round. DASH and Beyond Capacity are the same source.
sources.primary_evidence: §V-A2 chunks experts over multiple HBF dies/planes. §VI-E assigns each whole active expert to Direct or Relay and minimizes their concurrent completion bottleneck. §VI-A assumes four independently accessible subarrays per plane because exact HBF parallelism is undisclosed.
sources.our_inference: Expert striping across dies/planes and bottleneck-aware route distribution are existing ideas. No exact g12 omitted-group width rule or learned whole-row subset was established in inspected sections.
sources.limits: GPU weight delivery, not NAND GEMV. Assumed 16 dies×32 planes×4 subarrays, 4KiB pages and 3us read differ from AiF. Cannot import subarray independence or its timings.
sources.code: Uses an extension of LLMSimulator; no DASH-specific public artifact verified.

sources.title: FlashAccel: Leveraging High-Bandwidth Flash (HBF) for High-Throughput LLM Inference
sources.venue: arXiv preprint; no peer-reviewed venue verified
sources.read_depth: Original §III-B, §IV and §V-A/B read in earlier round; not comprehensively reread during this audit.
sources.primary_evidence: Coupled megaplanes share command control and block/page offsets. Model weights form megapages striped in execution order and packed across operator boundaries. Group granularity trades load balance against buffering.
sources.our_inference: Coupled hardware group granularity, geometry-aware packing and cross-operator compaction cannot be claimed as new general concepts.
sources.limits: GPU/HBM/HBF architecture with different plane count, buffering and transfer model; does not establish arbitrary independent 4-plane AiF input contexts or the exact expert complement rule.
sources.code: No author artifact verified; HBFSim is a separate project.

sources.title: DIAMoND: Dynamic Inference for Adaptive Edge MOE with Heterogeneous In-NAND and Near-DRAM Compute Architecture
sources.read_depth: Official abstract and metadata only, checked earlier; no legal author full text found in bounded prior searches. Full mapping algorithm NOT read.
sources.primary_evidence: Abstract describes mask-based mapping and heterogeneous in-NAND/near-DRAM inference.
sources.our_inference: Mask-based adaptive MoE mapping remains an unresolved direct prior. No claim that its masks are, or are not, the current 12-chip complement masks.
sources.limits: Exact physical row layout, replicas, plane contexts, CR usage and datatype not verified.
